text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Agricultural Finance Corporation approved 20,000 loan applications worth nearly Z$200 million for the small-scale farming sector for the current season, over 50 percent more than last year.
- The High Court reserved judgement on Wednesday in the application by Chitungwiza mayoral aspirant Fidelis George Mhashu to have the election of Andrew Jiri on September 9 last year nullified.

- Representatives of African political parties attending a Commonwealth roundtable summit in Botswana on democracy and good governance say a solution to the continent's political upheavals lies in the creation of stable structures that guarantee basic human rights.
- The government has approved the privatisation of the Commercial Bank of Zimbabwe Ltd in a landmark decision which will see it reducing its shareholding to just 20 percent.
- The take-over of African Associated Mines by an indigenous businessman last year was a straightforward business deal which is unlikely to be reversed.

- Vice President Joshua Nkomo last week threatened to resign from the government in protest against cabinet's apparent desire to award the second cellular telephone licence to a group of Harare-based politicians ahead of other prospective indigenous operators, including Strive Masiyiwa's Econet. Econet has been involved in lengthy court battles against the government to get a licence to operate the country's first private cellular telephone service.

- Zimtrade's board chaired by Harare businessman Paddy Zhanda has sent embattled chief executive Morrison Sifelani on indefinite leave pending a final decision on his fate, Zhanda and sources at the Harare-based trade promotion organisation said this week.

- The International Monetary Fund, in talks with Zimbabwe over funding for its economic reforms, hinted on Wednesday that it could resume financing the reforms if the government stamped down on its widening budget deficit in the 1997/98 financial budget.
